steps.text: In a large bowl, stir together the brown sugar, salt, pumpkin and cinnamon. Mix in the softened ice cream until well blended. Spoon into the pie crusts and place them in the freezer. Freeze for at least 3 hours before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Freezy Pumpkin Pie
raw_recipe.description: We made this recipe in third grade and the teacher sent a copy of the recipe home. I loved it so much I insisted my Mom make it, too. Ever since then it's become a Thanksgiving tradition each year. It has lasted the test of time because now I'm a mother of a third grader and we still make it! The pie requires no baking! And kids love it because it's made of ice cream.
raw_recipe.name: Easy Freezy Pumpkin Pie

recipeInstructions.text: In a large bowl, stir together the brown sugar, salt, pumpkin and cinnamon. Mix in the softened ice cream until well blended. Spoon into the pie crusts and place them in the freezer. Freeze for at least 3 hours before serving.

review.reviewBody: Very easy, very good. Would recommend using more pumpkin and less ice cream or more seasoning. Very mild and light.
I took others advice and added pumpkin pie spice along with the cinnamon to this recipe. I liked the flavor and it was not overbearing. Also finely chopped pecans added some texture and added flavor.

Love this! Why are folks getting too much filling for a 9” pie AND too little pumpkin flavor? I suspect they are using the full ice cream container, which is 1.5 qt! Use 2/3 of the normal container and it will be perfect. And while the recipe is awesome as is, I will say I prefer adding a touch of pumpkin pie spice, but that shouldn’t reflect on my opinion of this kid-friendly recipe.

It was very easy to make this. We did keep it in the freezer for a little while longer just to make sure it was fully frozen. It tasted delicious. We would recommend putting whipped cream on top to give it some additional flavor because it is an ice cream pie, of course. WE WILL FOR SURE BE MAKING THIS AGAIN!!!!

Nice way to get your pumpkin fix when it's too hot to turn your oven on! I also added 1/2 tsp pumpkin pie spice to bump up the spiciness. Used 1/2 a 2 litre container of Chapman's ice cream, good balance with pumpkin. Thanks for the recipe :)

Oh my goodness! Found this accidentally and I made 4 pies for our Canadian Thanksgiving. They were a hit and I will be making this again but I will not wait for Thanksgiving-- I will be making it more often. Used 1 1/2 cups pumpkin puree instead of 1 cup. Excellent recipe, thank you so much.

I'm giving it 5 stars for now, but may change it later. I read other reviews suggesting it needed more pumpkin & more spice. I'm not sure it did, but I added more. Since I added more pumpkin, I added more salt. Do not add more salt. If anything, short it a little. I also think I either overmixed it or over softened the ice cream. There was no spooning it into the pie crusts. However, these were my mistakes and i was in a rush finding things to bring to our Thanksgiving potluck when our oven died the morning before Thanksgiving. Additionally, this did not quite fill up both 9 inch crusts. Perhaps it would have been different if I hadn't over softened the ice cream? I think I may spread a little cool whip over the tops if I need to hide the difference and perhaps mask a little of the salt.

I never thought of pumpkin pie as a summer dessert before, but now I can thanks to this recipe. It was very easy to prepare and it tasted great. Next time I might try a little pumpkin pie spice. Thanks for sharing the recipe!
Easy and very tasty! I made it gluten-free by making my own crust using gluten-free cereal instead of graham crackers. It is a hit!
it was a great fun recipe the whole family enjoyed!

this pie is an excellent alternative as it saves oven space and can be made WAY ahead of time. i found that it tasted better, less sweet, more creamy, after a couple days in the freezer. big hit, even with those who preferred more savory foods.
yum,i added more creamy pumpkin & 1/2 & 1/2 cream ..peanut butter is good too.

I made this for my thanksgiving dessert. Eeverybody enjoted it but it seemed like it was missing something. I looked back over the recipe only to realize I forgot to mix the brown sugar in. So I plan on trying this recipe again WITH the brown sugar haha.
This is one of my favorite recipes even though I only eat pumpkin pie of nothing else is left. It's great; guests find it intriguing and tasty. Freezes well, as you might expect.
